samples.summary: Model-authored `scopedTitle` is interpolated into the report's markdown heading with no newline stripping, escaping or length bound, letting a verifier forge report structure
samples.evidence: `uiScopedTitle` (hunt-ui.mjs:286-291) only `.trim()`s the verifier-supplied string; `renderUiReport` then splices it straight into `` `### [${k.severity}] ${heading}` `` (hunt-ui.mjs:776) and the hunter's raw title into the new blockquote `` `> The hunter proposed this as **"${k.title}"** …` `` (hunt-ui.mjs:782). A verifier (or an explorer whose title is echoed in the blockquote) that emits a string containing `\n` breaks out of the heading/blockquote and can append arbitrary markdown to `.harness-reports/hunt-ui/report.md` — e.g. a second `### [critical] …` block with a fabricated `- **located by the verifiers:** \`packages/...:1\`` line, or prose that contradicts the seeded-run banner rendered at hunt-ui.mjs:715-729. Every other model string routed into this report is either validated (`groundedIn` must match `CITATION` and the persona `codeScope`, hunt-gate.mjs:576-581) or escaped/truncated (the drop table does `.replace(/\|/g,"\\|").slice(0,80)`, hunt-ui.mjs:832). Attack chain: a compromised/injected verifier response → forged findings in an artifact a maintainer files issues from. The same unescaped-heading pattern pre-exists for `k.title` at hunt.mjs:467, so this hunk widens an existing channel rather than creating the class.

samples.summary: New free-text channel from the source-reading verifier agent into report.md / run.json, which land in the CI-uploaded `.harness-reports/` artifact, guarded only by pattern-based redaction
samples.evidence: `record.scopedTitle = uiScopedTitle(record.claimed, verdicts)` (hunt-ui.mjs:1357) puts arbitrary verifier prose into the reported record. The verifier runs with `HUNT_TOOLS = ["Read","Grep","Glob"]` over the whole repo (hunt-ui.mjs:87, 602), so it can read `.env`-style files, fixtures and config. Before this change the only verifier-authored content reaching the report was `groundedIn`, which the gate constrains to `file:line` strings inside `codeScope` (hunt-gate.mjs:576-581); `reason` is deliberately not rendered. Now free text reaches `report.md` (hunt-ui.mjs:776/782) and `run.json` (hunt-ui.mjs:1036-1041), whose directory `.harness-reports/` is uploaded as a CI artifact (.github/workflows/ci.yml:84-85, .github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml:274-275). The only guard is `redactSecrets` (hunt-probe.mjs:41-53), which matches `wfb_`, JWTs, `Bearer` and `key=value` shapes plus the explicitly-listed `context.cfg.apiKey` — a credential that does not match those patterns (e.g. a bare hex/base64 token quoted in prose) passes through. I could not demonstrate an actual secret in the repo that survives redaction, hence low confidence; the impact if it happens is credential disclosure in a downloadable artifact.

samples.summary: The maintainer-facing headline is taken from whichever verifier happens to be first, with no unanimity requirement and no validation — a single model response now controls the reported claim
samples.evidence: `uiScopedTitle` returns `scoped[0]` — the first non-empty `scopedTitle` in verdict order (hunt-ui.mjs:287-290). The gate requires ALL verifiers to confirm on a named ground (hunt-gate.mjs:545-562), and requires every citation to pass `CITATION` + `codeScope` (hunt-gate.mjs:576-581), but nothing cross-checks the two verifiers' `scopedTitle`s against each other or against the evidence. So one verifier's framing — including one that narrowed to a *different, wrong* defect, or was steered by injected content in `context.issues`/`replayEvidence` fed into its prompt (hunt-ui.mjs:569-577) — becomes the heading a maintainer reads first and files from, while the second verifier's disagreeing scope is discarded silently. This is a weakening of the file's stated invariant that model prose reaching the report goes through a trusted check; `overclaimed` being non-gating is documented and deliberate, but the single-source headline is not discussed.

verdict.reason: The cited code exists as described (scopedTitle at hunt-ui.mjs:1357, rendered at 774-782, serialized into run.json at 1036-1041 under .harness-reports/ which CI uploads), but it is not a blocking security defect. (a) No attacker-controlled vector: the value is model prose with no external input path; the reviewer itself could not show any repo secret surviving redaction. (b) The documented egress guard is applied to this field identically to every other: renderUiReport returns redactSecrets(...) with per-candidate `extra` secrets (hunt-ui.mjs:842-845) and run.json is wrapped in redactSecrets with the live apiKey (hunt-ui.mjs:1038-1040). (c) The premise that this is a NEW free-text channel from a repo-reading agent is wrong: the explorer already holds the same Read/Grep/Glob grant (EXPLORER_TOOLS at hunt-ui.mjs:90) and its title/expected/observed prose already lands verbatim in report.md (hunt-ui.mjs:776/786/787) and run.json (1038) — the same shape exists in the baseline copy (.trusted/scripts/agent/hunt-ui.mjs:87,90,722-723,974). So scopedTitle adds no new exposure class, privilege, or unguarded path; at most this is a minor hardening remark about redactSecrets' pattern coverage, which is out of scope for a blocking security gate.
